papers_read.title_as_printed: Biomarker Extraction Based on Subspace Learning for the Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment Conversion (Li, Fang, Wang, Zhang, Hu; BioMed Research International 2021, 5531940)
Early progression detection from MCI to AD using multi-view MRI for enhanced assisted living (Rahim et al., Image and Vision Computing 157 (2025) 105491)

what_each_reports.P-185: ADNI 1.5 T baseline scans, 221 MCI (126 pMCI / 95 sMCI; conversion within 3 years); FreeSurfer regional cortical thickness and volume (78 AAL regions) projected into a subspace learned from 142 AD / 165 NC; 10-fold CV repeated 20 times. Best accuracy 69.37% (linear SVM; SEN 75.39%, SPE 61.23%, AUC 0.6951).
what_each_reports.P-41: 192 ADNI-1/GO/2 subjects with 3 T MPRAGE: 96 sMCI (MCI baseline to M48) vs a positive class of 81 pMCI (progressed between M18 and M48) plus 15 patients who already had AD; 132 2D slices per plane fed to EfficientNet/ConvNeXt/DenseNet with CBAM and a multi-head attention head; 71+71 training, 10+10 validation and 15+15 test subjects. Heterogeneous ensemble: accuracy 91.77 +/- 3.14%, SEN 87.69%, SPE 88.53%, AUC 92.87%.

quantity_a: Accuracy of pMCI (conversion within 3 years) vs sMCI from FreeSurfer ROI cortical thickness/volume features, ADNI 1.5 T MCI only, repeated 10-fold CV.
quantity_b: Accuracy of sMCI vs a positive class of pMCI (M18-M48 converters) plus established AD patients, from 2D multi-plane image slices through a CNN ensemble, ADNI 3 T, a 30-subject held-out test set.
incompatible_if_same: Unclear, and moot. P-185 gives no interval, and P-41's +/-3.14 is a spread over runs on a 30-subject test set. The two accuracies are far apart, but nothing in either paper states an estimate of the same quantity with uncertainty that excludes the other.

gates.task: nominal match (T2), but P-41's positive class includes 15 subjects who already had AD, so its label is not pure MCI conversion.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (P-185 1.5 T ADNI-1-type scans; P-41 3 T ADNI-1/GO/2 scans).
gates.validation_tier: match (both internal): P-185 uses 20x repeated 10-fold CV on 221 MCI; P-41 uses a single 30-subject held-out test.
gates.modality_family: match on structural MRI, but the input representation differs: pre-computed FreeSurfer ROI thickness/volume vectors vs 2D image slices. Precedent C-80 treats this as incommensurable representation.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both report accuracy, but the endpoints differ. P-185 is conversion within 3 years in MCI only. P-41 is M18-M48 converters plus AD patients against 48-month stables, so the population behind the positive label differs.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 91.77% accuracy and 92.87% AUC are below 0.97 (the 30-subject test set is small, but the automatic flag is not tripped).
independence: Both draw on ADNI; subject overlap between the P-185 MCI sample and P-41's ADNI-1/GO/2 sample is possible. Distinct author groups.
grounds: P-41's positive class mixes 81 pMCI with 15 established AD patients, while P-185's positive class is pMCI only, so the populations behind the 'conversion' label differ.
The horizons and definitions differ: conversion within 3 years (P-185) vs conversion between M18 and M48 against stables followed to M48 (P-41).
The input representations differ, as in precedent C-80: regional FreeSurfer thickness/volume features (P-185) vs 2D multi-plane image slices through a CNN ensemble (P-41).
The validation designs differ in a way that bears on the estimate: 20x10-fold CV on 221 MCI vs a single 30-subject test set.

evidence_quotes.quote: According to whether the MCI subjects will convert to AD or not within a given time period (i.e., 3 years), they are separated into two categories: progressive MCI (pMCI) and stable MCI (sMCI).
We use baseline MRI scans (1.5 T, 1:25 mm × 1:25 mm in-plane spatial resolution, 1.2 mm thick slices) of 528 subjects, which include 142 AD subjects, 165 NC subjects, and 221 MCI subjects.
The proposed biomarker achieved highest accuracy of 69.37% when using SVM classiﬁer with linear kernel.
Furthermore, we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.
The second group (pMCI) included 81 participants who were diagnosed with MCI at baseline but progressed to AD within 2.5 years, between month 18 (M18) and M48.

The MHA classifier in the same heterogeneous ensemble outperformed the LSTM with an accuracy of 91.77% ±3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% ±3.24, specificity of 88.53% ±3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% ±3.58.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-41: Acc 91 on T2' omits that P-41's positive class includes 15 established AD patients and that the test set is 15 + 15 subjects.
modality_family 'Neuroimaging' conceals the ROI-feature vs image-slice representation difference (the C-80 incommensurability pattern).
The P-185 registry row's Sample_N_Approx 528 counts AD and NC auxiliary subjects; the MCI classification sample is 221.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-41 result on MCI-only classes, with the AD patients removed and the same 3-year horizon, from ROI features or with a waiver recorded for representation, together with uncertainty excluding 69.37%. Neither paper provides this.
